name: Long Thoracic Nerve Palsy
definition: Neuropathy of the long thoracic nerve causing serratus anterior weakness and medial scapular winging.

investigations.principle: Electrodiagnostics help confirm localization; imaging is cause-directed.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Persistent severe palsy may require nerve or scapular surgery in selected cases.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa/Vata-neuropathy phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Neuropathy of the long thoracic nerve causing serratus anterior weakness and medial scapular winging.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
